`com.google.javascript.jscomp.GlobalNamespace.Name.canCollapseUnannotatedChildNames()`

Why:
- All failures show the compiler collapsing child properties of function-valued names that should remain uncollapsed when the function is aliased or escapes locally.
- Example failures:
  - `var a=function(){}; a.b=1; var c=a; ...` became `var a$b=1; ...`
  - `function a() {} var c = a; (function() {a.b = 0;})(); a.b;` became `var a$b; ... a$b`
  - `var a = {}; a.b = function() {}; a.b.c = 1; var d = a.b; ...` became `var a$b$c=1; ...`
- These all point to the pass deciding that child names of a function namespace can still be collapsed even when the function itself has aliases.
